In the matter of : Sagar Mallick. ...applicant/appellant.
 In Re: Application under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal
 Procedure, 1973 / Section 430(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik
 Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

And
 Mr. Jaydeep Biswas,
 Mr. Joy Chakraborty,
 Mr. Sandip Dinda,
 Mr. Kaushik Ghosh, ...for the Applicant/Appellant.
 Mrs. Amita Gaur, Sr. Govt. Adv.,
 Md. Y.A. Ismail, ...for the State.
 Mr. Debottam Das, ...for the de facto complainant.

Dictated by Arijit Banerjee, J.
In re : I.A. No. CRAN 2 of 2026 1.

The petitioner was convicted under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act read with Section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to suffer term imprisonment for sixteen years.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He now prays for suspension of sentence.
2. The petitioner says that he is in custody for more than six years and nine months.
He has been falsely implicated due to disputes between the two families.
The evidence-on-record does not support his conviction.
Hence, his prayer should be allowed.
3. Learned State counsel and learned advocate for the de facto complainant strongly oppose the prayer.
They say that the statement of the victim girl recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is duly corroborated by the evidence of the victim girl recorded before the learned trial Court.
Other prosecution witnesses also support the prosecution case.
The victim girl was only eleven years of age when the incident happened.
No leniency should be shown to the petitioner.
4. We have seen the evidence-on-record.
Prima facie, the medical evidence and the forensic evidence do not support the prosecution case.
PW-7 seems to be suggesting that the victim girl and the petitioner were together only on the verandah of the house and not inside the house.

We also see that the petitioner is in custody for a long time and has served out an appreciable part of the term Sagar Mallick vs Mr. Jaydeep Biswas on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81721841/
1 sentence of sixteen years.

sentences.text: 5. On the above considerations, we are inclined to allow this application for suspension of sentence.

6. It is thus ORDERED that the applicant/appellant namely, Sagar Mallick shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Kolkata subject to the condition that the petitioner shall remain within the geographical limits of Kolkata Municipal Corporation except for the purpose of attending court proceedings until further orders and shall not enter the jurisdiction of South Port police station and shall inform his present local address where he will be residing to the learned Trial Court and shall meet the Officer-in-Charge/Inspector- in-Charge of the local jurisdictional police station where he will be residing at present once in a fortnight till disposal of the appeal.

He shall be personally present or shall be represented by his counsel during hearing of the appeal and he shall surrender before the Trial Court as and when called for in connection with the present appeal.

7. The department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendent of the concerned Correctional Home for immediate release of the applicant/appellant unless he is wanted in connection with any other case.

8. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
9.
The application being I.A. No. CRAN 2 of 2026 is, accordingly, disposed of.
10. All parties shall act in terms of server copy of the order downloaded from the official website of this Court.
(Apurba Sinha Ray, J.)
